captions.detailed: This 3D-printable object is a stylized directional sign pointing towards the North Pole, designed in the shape of a classic pointing arrow with an irregular, decorative tail-end. The main body consists of a flat arrow plaque with a raised outer border, creating a recessed inner field. Extending outward from the sides of the arrow are decorative silhouettes, including a circular tab with a small mounting hole near one edge, and a detailed, multi-lobed ornamental shape on the opposite side.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric directional sign in OpenSCAD that displays the distance to the North Pole based on a user's latitude. The sign should feature a customizable pointing arrow body with a raised border, options to toggle the arrow direction (left or right), select the unit of measurement (miles or kilometers), and dynamically calculate and render the distance text.
captions.factory: The design is constructed using a module 'buildSign' which generates the base shape by linear extrusions of 2D polygons. The bottom layer is a red polygon extruded to a height of 6 units, followed by a white top layer extruded to 4 units. The white layer uses a 2D difference of a larger base polygon and several smaller inner polygons to create a raised border. The main program calculates the distance using the 'latitude' variable, formats the text dynamically, and positions it on top of the sign using the 'write' library. An 'arrow_direction' parameter mirrors the sign geometry, and a 'cylinder' subtraction creates a mounting hole in the circular tab.
